description: I’m Adam, an AI and technology researcher and builder interested in artificial intelligence, data science, simulation, and the design of intelligent systems that can solve real-world problems. I have experience working on AI research, multi-agent architectures, automation systems, and technology projects, and I enjoy turning complex ideas into practical prototypes.
summary: Earth Terminal is a Bloomberg-style terminal for a changing planet. Type a command  WMON, TREND, CO2, TEMP, ICE, EVENTS, HEAT, EARTH, ANALYST, ASK  and it answers the Trend Detective question for any place on Earth: what is changing, where, how much, and is it significant? TREND pulls real monthly NASA POWER data (MERRA-2 / GEOS, 1981–2025) for any variable and region, charts the time series, removes the seasonal cycle on request, and runs a Mann-Kendall test and a t-test at p < 0.05. The world monitor, CO2, temperature and sea-ice screens carry the headline indicators; EVENTS streams live NASA EONET natural events; HEAT maps significance-tested trends across 7 regions; EARTH puts the live events and earthquakes on an interactive 3D globe; ANALYST and ASK let a Gemini AI interpret the statistics and answer questions about the data. Demo: Rabat warmed +0.29 °C per decade (2000–2025), significant on both tests.
details:
Earth Terminal is a Bloomberg-style command terminal for planet Earth. Type a function code WMON, TREND, CO2, TEMP, ICE, EVENTS, HEAT, EARTH, ANALYST, ASK or click a sector key, and the terminal answers the challenge's four questions for any place on Earth: what is changing, where, how much per decade, and whether the change is statistically significant.

In TREND you pick a variable (temperature, rainfall, humidity, wind, sunlight, pressure), a place (region preset or any latitude/longitude), and a period (1981–2025). The terminal fetches the monthly series live from NASA POWER (MERRA-2 / GEOS), charts it with a trend line, and tests it with an OLS slope per decade, a 95% confidence interval, a t-test, a Mann-Kendall test, and a Theil-Sen slope — then gives a plain-language verdict. Three demo investigations show it working: Rabat warmed 0.29 °C per decade (2000–2025, significant on both tests), Svalbard 0.77 °C per decade, and Sahel rainfall rose 0.095 mm/day per decade. EVENTS streams live NASA EONET natural events, USGS earthquakes and the Kp space-weather index; HEAT maps significance-tested trends across seven regions; EARTH plots live events on an interactive 3D globe with a climate-anomalies panel. ANALYST and ASK use Google Gemini (the user's own key) to interpret the statistics and answer questions only from the terminal's own data. The TREND series can be downloaded as CSV to check the numbers.

The benefit is that anyone a student, a teacher, a citizen — can test a climate claim about their own town with real data and real statistics, in seconds, with no install and no login. The intended impact is climate literacy: evidence instead of headlines, and a tool people can reuse for any place they care about.

It was built as a single self-contained web page in HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Three.js for the 3D globe, live calls to the NASA POWER, NASA EONET, USGS and NOAA SWPC public APIs, and Gemini 3.8 Flash for the AI screens. No hardware and no server: everything runs in the browser.

The creative idea is the metaphor itself a trading terminal, but the asset being tracked is the planet plus a detective workflow (pick a variable, a place, a period, read the verdict) and an AI that is only allowed to speak from the data on screen. Honesty came first: if a live feed fails, the terminal falls back to clearly labelled cached data, never invented numbers; the AI key lives only in the user's browser, never in the page; and no NASA branding is used anywhere.
